regime_context: The detector shows a broad AI/semiconductor leadership cluster (AI Infra rank 1, Cybersecurity 2, WFE 3) with the absolute-trend gate identifying these as eligible; the one validated edge here is the trend-gate's drawdown/shake-out control, not return forecasting. Note the proxy overlap: SMH appears for AI Infra, WFE, AI Semis, and Memory/Storage, and XLK appears for Non-AI Tech, EW Tech, and AI Software, so several 'themes' are not independently scorable. Rotation is narrowing (43% eligible) with AI Infra's lead margin over Cybersecurity at 0.65 and no one-narrative lock; crowding is flagged on Cybersecurity and Non-AI Tech only as a size-down caution, not a fade.
emerging_watch: Watch whether AI Software & Platforms (rank 20, XLK proxy, breadth 0.706, crowding z 0.76) begins to rise in rank toward the leader cluster while staying trend-gate eligible — a condition that would retire the watch is its score remaining below 0.4 and rank outside the top 12 over the next 10 trading days.

theses.subject: AI Infrastructure
theses.thesis: AI Infra leads the board (rank 1, score 2.30), is trend-gate eligible, shows broad participation (breadth 0.917) and is not crowded (z 0.84). The trend-gate is the only validated leg here, and it is already engaged; my directional lean is a muted continuation-follow, not a claim the rank predicts returns. Durability bar 0.72 is adequate but val_state 'fading' suggests I keep the horizon short.
evidence: rank 1 with score 2.298 and eligible == true (absolute-trend gate engaged)
rotation margin 0.65 over leader and 0.43 eligible-frac still supports leadership, though narrowing
theses.dissent: Most of the top names share the SMH proxy, so AI Infra could simply be a concentrated semiconductor beta trade; val_state 'fading' plus a narrowing rotation means the leadership itself may be in the late stage rather than the middle.

falsifier.text: SMH falls below its own 20-day trailing average while that average is declining by the check-by date

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity is trend-gate eligible, shows the strongest trend-health signature in the top ranks (hurst_tag 'trend', breadth 1.0, durability bar 0.85) and a high score of 1.65. Crowding z 1.95 is a size-down caution only, not a fade; the condition I would want is trend continuation without a breadth breakdown.
evidence: hurst_tag 'trend' with breadth 1.0 and durability_bar 0.85 (most cohesive top theme)
crowding_z 1.95, crowded == true (size-down caution, per guardrails not a sell/fade)
theses.dissent: Crowding is elevated (z 1.95, top-decile), which per the detector carries no forward basket-timing edge but does mark the theme as late-attention; a crowded trend theme with a separate AI-infra leader above it is the classic place to be caught on an unwind.

falsifier.text: CIBR lags SPY by more than 5% over the check window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Non-AI Tech & Hardware
theses.thesis: Non-AI Tech is trend-gate eligible with breadth 1.0 and durability bar 0.89 but is crowded (z 1.01) and, more importantly, shares the XLK proxy with two other themes (EW Tech and AI Software), so the theme is not uniquely scorable and is dominated by a crowding flag in a market where the edge is de-risking not selection.
theses.dissent: The trend-health metrics (breadth 1.0, durability 0.89, hurst 'trend') are among the strongest in the table; avoiding a coherent, eligible trend costs participation if the AI complex keeps broadening into non-AI hardware.

falsifier.text: XLK outperforms SPY by 5% or more over the check window before the check-by date
